blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
A certain class of business problem resists simple diagnosis. The symptoms are visible and uncomfortable, but the underlying causes are distributed across several functions, partially hidden by organisational politics, and frequently mis-described by the people closest to them. These are the problems that mediocre analysis merely rearranges, rather than solves.

Serious diagnosis begins with a deliberate pause. Before any explanation is entertained, the investigator collects the facts in neutral language — what happened, when, and how that compares to what was expected. That simple discipline prevents the most common failure: choosing an explanation first, and then fitting the evidence around it.

Only then can the real work begin: generating multiple plausible explanations, stress-testing each against the evidence, and resisting the comfortable pull of the one that is politically convenient. The best diagnosticians are often those willing to conclude, patiently, that the real cause is something nobody wanted to hear.

items.q: According to the text, what do mediocre analysts do with this class of problem?
options: They document it thoroughly
They solve it faster than expected
They rearrange it rather than solve it
They escalate it to senior leadership
items.why: "the problems that mediocre analysis merely rearranges, rather than solves."

items.q: Why does the investigator collect facts in neutral language first?
options: To avoid choosing an explanation and then fitting the evidence around it
To identify who is to blame
To speed up the final decision
To satisfy the audit team
items.why: "That simple discipline prevents the most common failure: choosing an explanation first, and then fitting the evidence around it."

items.q: What makes these causes hard to see, according to the text?
options: They only appear in external markets
They are always financial in nature
They change constantly over time
They are distributed, hidden by politics, and mis-described by those closest to them
items.why: Parágrafo 1: causas distribuídas entre funções, escondidas pela política e mal descritas por quem está mais perto.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: The most convenient explanation deserves the most suspicion
Good diagnosis sometimes reaches an unwelcome conclusion
Facts should be gathered before explanations are proposed
Once you find a plausible cause, stop looking and act on it
items.why: Inferência: o texto defende gerar VÁRIAS explicações e testá-las — parar na primeira plausível é justamente o erro que ele critica.

items.q: The final sentence about a cause "nobody wanted to hear" suggests that…
options: leadership always resists analysis
most problems have no real cause
diagnosis should be delegated to outsiders
the correct diagnosis is often politically inconvenient
items.why: Inferência: a coragem de concluir o que ninguém queria ouvir implica que a verdade costuma ir contra a conveniência política.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry apresentando as conclusões da sua investigação. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, let me walk you through where the margin actually went, because it isn't where any of you thought.

When I started, commercial blamed rising costs, finance blamed a shift in product mix, and operations insisted it was neither. So I ignored all three stories and just pulled the raw numbers — order by order, month by month. What that showed was uncomfortable. Costs were essentially flat. Mix moved, but only enough to explain about a fifth of the drop.

The bulk of it sat somewhere nobody was looking. We had quietly been granting larger discounts to retain a handful of big accounts, and because that decision was spread across three regional desks, no single team ever saw the total. Consequently, everyone assumed it was someone else's problem.

Now, I'll be honest — the convenient answer would have been to say costs, present a savings plan, and move on. But that would have fixed nothing. The real cause is a pricing discipline gap, and owing to how the discounts were distributed, it stayed invisible for two quarters. My recommendation is that we consolidate discount authority and revisit it monthly. It won't be popular, but it's the honest read of the evidence.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What did Harry do with the three teams' explanations?
options: He averaged the three explanations
He set them aside and pulled the raw numbers himself
He asked each team to prove its case
He accepted the finance team's version
items.why: "I ignored all three stories and just pulled the raw numbers — order by order, month by month."

items.q: According to Harry, how much of the margin drop did product mix actually explain?
options: Exactly half
About a fifth
None of it
Almost all of it
items.why: "Mix moved, but only enough to explain about a fifth of the drop."

items.q: Why did no single team notice the real cause?
options: The numbers were reported only once a year
The data was deliberately concealed by finance
The discount decisions were spread across three regional desks, so no one saw the total
Operations refused to share its figures
items.why: "because that decision was spread across three regional desks, no single team ever saw the total."

items.q: What does Harry imply about the "convenient answer" of blaming costs?
options: It was suggested by the operations team
It would have looked tidy but solved nothing
It was what the evidence pointed to
It would have been faster and more accurate
items.why: Inferência: ele diz que apresentar um plano de custos e seguir em frente "would have fixed nothing" — conveniente, mas falso.

items.q: How would you best describe Harry's approach to the diagnosis?
options: Reliant on the intuition of the three teams
Focused mainly on assigning blame
Evidence-led, even at the cost of an unpopular conclusion
Politically cautious, choosing the least controversial cause
items.why: Inferência: ele reconhece que a conclusão não será popular, mas a defende como "the honest read of the evidence".

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The team fell into confirmation bias, dismissing any data that contradicted their first theory." Confirmation bias is…
options: the practice of double-checking every figure
a formal step in an audit process
a bias toward newer information over older data
the tendency to favour evidence that supports what you already believe
items.why: Confirmation bias = viés de confirmação: buscar/aceitar só o que confirma a hipótese inicial.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Before proposing fixes, we did a full ___ of the process, breaking it into its component steps."
options: decomposition
diagnosis
symptom
hypothesis
items.why: Decomposition = decomposição: quebrar o problema nas suas partes constituintes.

items.q: "We reasoned from first principles rather than copying last year's playbook." This means they…
options: relied on the most senior person's opinion
followed the established best practice
built the argument up from fundamental truths
used the first explanation available
items.why: First principles = princípios fundamentais: raciocinar a partir das verdades básicas, não por analogia.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Fixing the visible complaint is only ___ relief; the root cause is untouched."
options: symptomatic
convenient
patient
distributed
items.why: Symptomatic = sintomático: trata o sintoma, não a causa.

items.q: "A hypothesis tree helped us map every possible cause branch by branch." A hypothesis tree is…
options: a ranking of the team's preferred conclusions
a structured breakdown of possible explanations into branches
a list of approved solutions
a timeline of when the problem appeared
items.why: Hypothesis tree = árvore de hipóteses: estrutura ramificada que força considerar todas as explicações possíveis.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem quando se investiga um problema. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "We managed to rule out rising costs as the cause." To rule out means to…
options: postpone investigating
eliminate as a possibility
confirm as the main cause
report to the board
items.why: Rule out = descartar, eliminar uma explicação com base na evidência.

items.q: "Once we saw the discount data, we had to go back to the drawing board." This means they…
options: presented the findings publicly
started their thinking again from scratch
blamed another department
approved the original plan
items.why: Go back to the drawing board = voltar à estaca zero, recomeçar o raciocínio do início.

items.q: "Finance kept trying to explain away the gap as a one-off." To explain away means to…
options: document it carefully
analyse it in full detail
dismiss something by giving a reassuring reason
escalate it urgently
items.why: Explain away = minimizar/afastar um problema arranjando uma justificativa conveniente.

items.q: "Let's not jump to conclusions — let's get to the bottom of this first." To get to the bottom of means to…
options: summarise it briefly
find the true underlying cause
delegate it downward
close the investigation
items.why: Get to the bottom of = chegar à real causa de fundo de algo.

items.q: "Consolidating discount authority won't be popular, but we have to follow through on it." To follow through means to…
options: soften its impact
announce it to the regions
revisit the decision later
carry it fully to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar a cabo, executar até o fim o que foi decidido.
